title: Can you buy Tesla Optimus?
description: No. Optimus Gen 2 is Coming Soon. The $20,000 to $30,000 band is an estimate, and Tesla has not opened a checkout.
summary: You cannot buy Optimus Gen 2. Tesla has no cart and no home price. The catalog estimate is not a store price.
shortAnswer: No. Optimus Gen 2 is Coming Soon on HomeBotRadar. Tesla has not published a store price or opened a reservation. The $20,000 to $30,000 figure is an at-scale target, not a checkout.
content:
You cannot buy Optimus Gen 2. The catalog status is Coming Soon. There is no reservation page, no deposit, and no country list. The price field shows $20,000 to $30,000 because that is the at-scale target Tesla has talked about. The price status is an estimate. It is not a shop price, and it will not hold a unit for you.

## No checkout

Tesla's AI page is the public home for the robot, and it still does not sell one. The October 21, 2026 shareholder update is the source for this answer. It says Optimus production has started at Fremont, on lines that used to build other vehicles, and that the ramp is early. California is the early site. Texas is still being built. The letter does not name a version, a unit count, a home ship date, or a dollar price.

That is why the catalog and the letter can both be true. Production for Tesla's own use is not the same thing as a product you can order. The first robots off a line can stay inside the company. HomeBotRadar does not turn a factory sentence into a cart.

## The $20,000 to $30,000 target

Treat the band as a goal for a later, larger run. It has shown up in Tesla comments for years. It has never shown up as a list price next to a buy button. Tax, shipping, a required plan, and which version you would get are all unpublished. If a store price appears, the robot page is the place it will change. Until then, quoting $20,000 as if you could pay it today is wrong.

Optimus Gen 2 is about 173 cm on the catalog sheet. Many of the other specs are still unconfirmed, because Tesla shares little outside demos and the shareholder letters. A height on a profile is not a delivery window.

## A robot you can buy

If the search is "humanoid I can order," start with Unitree G1. It is Buy Now at $13,500. The shop is often backordered, and the EDU version is quote-only, but the base unit has a live cart. That is the gap the compare page is for: /compare/optimus-gen2-vs-unitree-g1.

The full humanoid set, including Coming Soon rows, is on /rankings/best-humanoid-robots. Optimus stays on that list so the status is visible. It is also on /knowledge/buying with the other answers about carts that do not exist. Figure 02 is a different case: that generation is already retired, which is covered at /knowledge/figure-02-retired-what-to-order. NEO Gamma is the US home pre-order, at $20,000 or $499 a month, and that price is a real order page rather than a target. Read it at /knowledge/neo-gamma-cost-and-ship-date.

Open /wizard when you care more about the job than the brand. It will not offer Optimus Gen 2 as something you can pay for this week.

title: What does NEO Gamma cost, and when does it ship?
description: NEO Gamma is a US pre-order at $20,000, or $499 a month, with a $200 deposit. The order page still says 2026 US delivery.
summary: Early access is $20,000 or $499 a month. A $200 deposit holds the place. Delivery is still a 2026 US pre-order, not a ship confirmation.
shortAnswer: NEO Gamma is a US pre-order. Early access ownership is $20,000, or $499 a month, and the order page asks for a $200 refundable deposit. 1X still says US deliveries start in 2026. That is not a date for your address.
content:
NEO Gamma costs $20,000 to own on the early-access plan, or $499 a month if you subscribe instead. Both numbers are on the 1X order page, and both are confirmed on the catalog row. A $200 deposit is refundable and holds a place in line. It is not the full price, and it is not proof that a robot has left the factory for your house.

HomeBotRadar keeps the catalog name NEO Gamma. 1X now brands the consumer product as NEO and describes it as the successor to earlier Gamma and Beta hardware. The price below is for that consumer pre-order, not for a separate Gamma leftover.

## The $20,000 pre-order

The $20,000 path is ownership. The order page includes a 3-year warranty and puts those buyers ahead for 2026 US delivery. Tax and shipping are the usual extras a checkout adds. The catalog price field is $20,000 because that is the ownership number, not the monthly plan. If you compare robots by the price column alone, you are looking at the buy path.

The hardware sheet on the same order page lists about 168 cm, about 30 kg, and about 4 hours of runtime on an 842 Wh pack. Hands are listed at 22 degrees of freedom each. Those specs are confirmed from that sheet when the robot page matches it. They do not mean every chore in a demo video is autonomous on day one. 1X describes Expert Mode, a scheduled remote operator, for tasks the robot has not learned yet.

## $499 a month

The subscription is $499 a month and is scheduled for later delivery than the ownership plan. Read it as a lease of the early-access robot, not as a cheaper way to get the same 2026 priority. The $200 deposit still applies. Over a few years the monthly plan costs more than $20,000, which is the point of checking both numbers before you pay the deposit.

There is no public price for a second country. The catalog countries list is the United States. A shopper outside the US should treat the page as a US offer until 1X says otherwise.

## A 2026 window, not a doorstep date

The order page still says US deliveries start in 2026. The robot page was rechecked on November 3, 2026, and that sentence was still there. An April 30 factory note said units coming off the line were prioritized for internal home testing. The order page has not announced that a customer shipment has started. "Starts in 2026" can still mean late in the year, and it can still slip. Do not read the deposit as a delivery appointment.

## The humanoid you can cart today

Unitree G1 is Buy Now at $13,500. It is a smaller research and education humanoid, often backordered, and it is not the same home product. The price gap and the status gap are both on /compare/neo-gamma-vs-unitree-g1. Every humanoid we track, including ones you cannot buy, is on /rankings/best-humanoid-robots.

This answer sits on /knowledge/price. Whether Tesla will sell Optimus Gen 2 at all is a different question, answered at /knowledge/can-you-buy-tesla-optimus. Figure 02 is already retired, so it is not the fallback if this pre-order is too expensive. That case is at /knowledge/figure-02-retired-what-to-order. Open /wizard when price is only one of the filters you care about.

title: Figure 02 is retired. What can you order?
description: Figure 02 is Discontinued. Most of the fleet is gone, and there is still no price. NEO Gamma and Unitree G1 are the humanoids you can order.
summary: Figure 02 is not for sale. Order NEO Gamma at $20,000 or Unitree G1 at $13,500. There is no Figure 02 cart to wait on.
shortAnswer: Nothing from the Figure 02 line. Figure said on September 30, 2026 that most of that fleet is gone, with a few units left in storage. You can pre-order NEO Gamma at $20,000, or buy Unitree G1 at $13,500.
content:
You cannot order Figure 02. The catalog status is Discontinued, and the price is Unknown. Figure's September 30, 2026 note is the source for this answer. The company said keeping the F.02 fleet no longer made sense as the newer fleet grew. Most units are gone. A few remain in storage at headquarters. Storage is not a waitlist, and it is not a refurbished sale.

## September 30, 2026

Before that date, Figure 02 was already not a home product. It walked on two legs, used two hands, and showed up in workforce pilots, including a long run at BMW's Spartanburg plant. Those deployments were real, which is why the reality score did not fall to zero. They were not a checkout. There was no public list price before the retirement, and the decommission note did not add one. Older estimates that floated $18,000 or $20,000 were dropped from the catalog because no official price was ever published.

HomeBotRadar still keeps the profile so the retired generation can be compared with robots that have an order path. The status column is the point. A discontinued row is context. It is not an offer, and a higher score on an old demo does not bring the fleet back.

## NEO Gamma and Unitree G1

If you wanted a humanoid you can actually start, two catalog rows are the current paths.

NEO Gamma is the US home pre-order. Early access ownership is $20,000, or $499 a month, with a $200 refundable deposit. The order page still talks about 2026 US delivery. It does not promise a week. The side-by-side with the retired robot is /compare/figure-02-vs-neo-gamma. The dollar details live at /knowledge/neo-gamma-cost-and-ship-date.

Unitree G1 is Buy Now at $13,500. It is about 132 cm tall and sold mainly for research and education. The shop cart is live and often backordered. EDU pricing is quote-only. It is the clearest "add to cart" humanoid on the site, and it is a different kind of product from a home chore pre-order. Read both before you treat them as substitutes.

## Not a hidden Figure checkout

Figure has talked about a newer generation. That robot is not a HomeBotRadar row with a price and a status you can order against, so this answer does not send you there. Waiting on Figure 02 itself will not turn into a shipment. Optimus Gen 2 is also not the replacement: it is Coming Soon, with an estimate instead of a store price. That question is at /knowledge/can-you-buy-tesla-optimus.

Robots you can buy or pre-order, including the non-humanoids, are on /rankings/best-home-robots. This page sits with the other cart answers at /knowledge/buying. Open /wizard when the task matters more than the brand you searched for.

title: Does Vector 2.0 need a subscription?
description: Vector 2.0 is $249.99. Hey Vector and the AI chat need a paid plan, from $11.99 a month. The robot still rolls without it.
summary: Yes for voice. The robot is $249.99. ChatGPT voice is $11.99 a month or $99.99 a year. Claude is a second plan. The first weeks are free.
shortAnswer: The robot does not. Voice does. Vector 2.0 is $249.99 on anki.bot. Hey Vector, ChatGPT, and Claude need a membership. ChatGPT is $11.99 a month or $99.99 a year. Claude is $14.99 a month or $139.99 a year. A new order includes a free first stretch, listed as 28 days on the product page and 30 days in the help center.
content:
Vector 2.0 costs $249.99 to take home. That price does not include the voice you see in the ads. The product page says Vector requires a paid subscription for voice commands, and that every new Vector includes the first 28 days free. Without the plan, the robot can still move and use Alexa. Hey Vector gets no answer, because that command is served from the Vector cloud.

## The plans on the membership page

The subscription page lists ChatGPT at $11.99 a month and $99.99 a year. The help center, updated September 21, 2026, adds the Claude backend at $14.99 a month or $139.99 a year. One membership covers one robot. You pick the backend in the Stratus account, enter the 8-character serial number, and pay through Stripe. Annual plans include priority support. The help center also says the first 30 days are free on a new order from anki.bot or Amazon, if you email support with the serial number and the order number. The product page says 28 days. Those two official sentences do not match. HomeBotRadar keeps both, and does not pick a winner.

Activation can take up to 24 hours, and longer if you powered Vector on before you bought the plan. The help center says a Clear User Data reset can skip that wait on a new robot. Firmware usually follows within 48 to 72 hours. Billing renews on its own. Annual customers get an email 72 hours before the charge.

## The robot without a plan

The help center is explicit about the unpaid robot. Alexa voice commands and autonomous behavior still work. Hey Vector and the AI connection do not. You still need a Stratus account to set the robot up, even with no membership. The product page puts the same idea in shorter words: without the subscription, Vector is not connected to the cloud, which is where the action happens.

The catalog price stays $249.99, confirmed, Buy Now. Open-box colors show up on the store at lower figures from time to time. Those are not the catalog price. Countries on the catalog row include the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany, France, and Australia.

## Loona does not use this plan

Loona is the pet people compare with Vector 2.0. The catalog price is $439, confirmed, and the KEYi product page currently shows Loona Petbot Premium at $409 against a $529 list. Core pet play on Loona is not sold as a Vector-style membership. The gap is the point of /compare/loona-vs-vector-2. One robot is a desk companion with a cloud voice plan. The other is a wheeled pet with a camera, a dock, and a store price that moves with promos.

Desk and pet rows that you can order today are on /rankings/best-robot-pets. The EMO price, another small companion, is at /knowledge/how-much-is-emo. This page sits with the other money answers at /knowledge/price. Open /wizard when the job matters more than the brand.

title: Which home robots climb stairs?
description: Spot lists a 300 mm step height. It is not a home cart. Unitree G1 and NEO Gamma do not publish a stair rating.
summary: Spot can take a 300 mm step. It is an enterprise robot with an estimated price. The home humanoids you can order do not publish stairs.
shortAnswer: Spot is the catalog robot with a published step height: 300 mm, and a max slope of ±30 degrees, on the Boston Dynamics spec table. It is not sold as a living-room pet. The catalog price is an estimate, about $74,500 or more, and sales are limited. Unitree G1 and NEO Gamma do not publish a stair rating on their product pages.
content:
A staircase is a different problem from a flat hallway. The catalog robot that publishes a step height is Spot. On the Boston Dynamics product page, the locomotion table lists a max step height of 300 mm (11.8 in) and a max slope of ±30 degrees. Walking height sits around 610 mm, and the robot weighs about 33.8 kg with a battery. That is a stair-sized step for a typical indoor flight. It is also an inspection platform, not a chore robot for a family.

## Spot is not a home checkout

Boston Dynamics sells Spot to factories, energy sites, labs, construction, and public safety. The page talks about autonomous charging, inspection packages, and a payload of about 20 kg. It does not offer a living-room price. HomeBotRadar keeps the last public Explorer-kit figure, about $74,500 in 2020 for the robot, batteries, charger, and tablet. The price status is an estimate. A configured robot with an arm and software costs more, and the company quotes qualified buyers. Commercial, industrial, and academic customers are the stated market. A homeowner who wants Spot for the stairs is asking for an enterprise sale.

## The humanoids you can order

Unitree G1 is Buy Now at $13,500. The official spec page lists a standing height of about 132 cm, a weight of about 35 kg, a knee torque figure, and a depth camera plus 3D LiDAR. It does not list a step height, a slope limit, or a stair mode. A missing line is not a promise that the robot will take your staircase, and it is not a lab test either. Treat the G1 as a compact humanoid with a cart, often backordered, until Unitree prints a stair number.

NEO Gamma is the US home pre-order, at $20,000 or $499 a month. The order page is about early access, a deposit, and 2026 US delivery. It does not rate the robot for stairs. A home humanoid that can walk on a show floor still has to be rated for your steps, your landings, and what happens if it falls. That rating is not on the page.

## Apartments and the list that leaves humanoids out

If the home has stairs, do not read a two-leg body as a yes. The apartment ranking at /rankings/best-apartment-home-robots is the cut for robots you can order in a flat, and it leaves humanoids off on purpose. Compare the two humanoids that do have an order path at /compare/neo-gamma-vs-unitree-g1. The G1 price is at /knowledge/how-much-is-the-unitree-g1. Where NEO Gamma ships is at /knowledge/where-does-neo-gamma-ship. This answer lives with the other capability pages at /knowledge/capabilities. Open /wizard when the room and the job matter more than a stair rumor.

title: How much is the Unitree G1?
description: Unitree G1 is $13,500, confirmed, Buy Now. The shop is often backordered. EDU pricing is quote-only.
summary: The base Unitree G1 is $13,500 before tax and shipping. The cart is live and often backordered. EDU is a quote.
shortAnswer: Unitree G1 is $13,500 on the catalog, and that figure is confirmed. Status is Buy Now, with limited availability because the shop is often backordered. Tax and shipping are extra. The EDU version is quote-only. The $13,500 line is the base robot, not a package with dexterous hands.
content:
Unitree G1 is the humanoid with a live base price. HomeBotRadar lists $13,500, confirmed. The product page and the UniStore shop are the two official doors. The shop cart is the reason the status is Buy Now rather than Pre-order. Units are frequently backordered, so limited availability is the honest second line. A backorder is still a cart. It is not a deposit on a robot that has no price.

## The $13,500 base

The base G1 is the standard model. Unitree's spec table puts the standing size near 132 cm tall, about 45 cm wide, and about 20 cm thick, at roughly 35 kg with the battery. The base joint count is 23. EDU versions run up to about 43 joints and add a development stack. Arm load is about 2 kg on the base model and about 3 kg on EDU. Battery life on the catalog sheet is about two hours. The $13,500 figure is the base robot before tax and shipping. EDU pricing is a sales quote, not a second sticker on the same page. Quote the EDU only after Unitree sends the number.

Hands are the usual place the total moves. A dexterous hand is an option on the higher trims, not a part you should assume is inside $13,500. If a configurator adds a hand, a battery, or a shipping lane, the checkout number is the one that matters that day. The catalog number stays the confirmed base until Unitree changes the shop price.

## The home humanoid next to it

NEO Gamma is the other humanoid shoppers put beside the G1. It is a US pre-order at $20,000 to own, or $499 a month, with a $200 refundable deposit. That is a home product with a 2026 delivery window. The G1 is a smaller research and education humanoid that you can try to buy now. The price gap and the job gap are both on /compare/neo-gamma-vs-unitree-g1.

Countries on the G1 catalog row are the United States, China, Japan, and Germany. A shopper outside that list should read the shop's own shipping rules before treating $13,500 as a delivered price. The full humanoid set, including robots you cannot cart, is on /rankings/best-humanoid-robots. The NEO price and ship window are at /knowledge/neo-gamma-cost-and-ship-date. Stairs are a separate question, answered at /knowledge/which-home-robots-climb-stairs, because the G1 spec page does not print a step height. This page sits at /knowledge/price. Open /wizard when you care which job the robot is for.

title: What does ElliQ cost?
description: The catalog lists ElliQ at $250. The membership page leases the device: $249 to start, then $59 a month, $588 a year, or $936 for 24 months.
summary: ElliQ is a US lease. The catalog price is $250. The membership page charges $249 to start, then a plan from $59 a month.
shortAnswer: ElliQ is a membership, not a robot you own. The catalog price is $250, confirmed, Buy Now, in the United States. The membership page bills a $249 lease initiation with the plan you pick: $59 a month, $588 prepaid for 12 months, or $936 prepaid for 24 months. The device goes back when the membership ends.
content:
ElliQ is the elder-care companion with a price that looks small until you read the lease. HomeBotRadar lists $250, confirmed. The membership page is more precise. A one-time lease initiation of $249 is billed today, together with the plan. Monthly is $59. Twelve months are $588, paid up front. Twenty-four months are $936, paid up front. The page presents the longer plans as $49 and $39 a month. Those are the prepaid totals divided by the months, not a bill that arrives every month at the lower rate.

## You lease the lamp

The membership page says the device is leased because ElliQ is an ongoing service. The fee covers the device, shipping and returns, setup help, software updates, a lifetime hardware warranty, the caregiver app, and support for as long as you stay a member. When the membership ends, the hardware goes back. The $249 initiation is not a down payment on a robot you keep. The catalog's $250 is the same class of number as that initiation fee, rounded to the tracked sticker. If the page and the catalog ever split by more than a dollar, the catalog keeps $250 until an editor changes the row, and this answer will still name the live membership figures.

Annual and 24-month plans include a 30-day risk-free trial. The monthly plan does not. The page also says you can move from monthly to a longer plan later. Shipping on the offer is US. The catalog countries list is the United States. A shopper outside the US should not treat the checkout as local. Call the number on the membership page if a state program or a health plan offers ElliQ at no retail cost. That path is not the $249 checkout, and it is not on the catalog price.

## FIDI is not this lease

FIDI is the other elder-care robot on the compare. It is a tabletop feeding arm from Poland, on a waitlist, with a price of TBA. It is not a membership lamp and it is not a substitute you can order tonight. The useful contrast is at /compare/elliq-vs-fidi: one robot has a US lease with published dollars, and the other has no public price yet.

Elder-care rows are collected at /rankings/best-elder-care-robots. Doova, the wheeled senior companion that is still Coming Soon, is at /knowledge/is-doova-for-sale. This answer sits at /knowledge/price. Open /wizard if the person who will live with the robot matters more than the brand on the lease.

title: How much is EMO?
description: EMO is $279, confirmed, Buy Now. It stays on a desk. It does not walk the house.
summary: EMO is $279 on the catalog, confirmed and Buy Now. It is a desk robot, not a pet that follows you.
shortAnswer: EMO is $279, confirmed, and the status is Buy Now. It is a desktop companion from Living AI. It rolls on a table. It does not patrol the house. The catalog ships it to the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Germany.
content:
EMO is the small desk robot with a face and wheels. HomeBotRadar lists it at $279, confirmed, Buy Now, available. The product page and the Living AI store are the official doors. The catalog figure is the one this answer quotes. If the store shows a colorway, a bundle, or a shipping add-on, that checkout total can sit above $279. The tracked price stays $279 until the row changes.

## A desk, not a hallway

EMO chats, plays simple games, and can reach some smart-home devices through the Living AI app. It stays on a flat surface and rolls in small circles. It does not walk around a home, climb anything, or carry laundry. That limit is why it belongs on the desktop ranking rather than next to a humanoid. Battery, a specific country tax, and which color is in stock are store questions. The catalog countries are the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Germany. A white colorway and the standard unit can carry different store labels. Compare the unit, not the photo.

People shop EMO when they want a companion without a humanoid budget and without a pet that needs floor space. The price sits in the same band as other small robots you can cart this week. Living AI sells it as a product you can order, not as a lease and not as a kit you assemble for an afternoon. If a bundle adds a case or a spare part, that line is extra. The robot on the catalog sheet is the $279 unit. Color and a case do not change the tracked price.

## Vector 2.0 is the subscription cousin

Vector 2.0 is $249.99 for the robot, and voice is extra. Hey Vector needs a membership, from $11.99 a month or $99.99 a year on the ChatGPT plan. EMO's catalog price is a single sticker. Vector's sticker is the hardware, and the cloud voice is a second bill. The side-by-side is /compare/emo-companion-vs-vector-2. EMO does not ask for that second bill on the catalog row.

Whether Vector's plan is required for the features in the ads is answered at /knowledge/does-vector-need-a-subscription. Desktop robots with a confirmed price under $500, including EMO, are on /rankings/best-desktop-robots-under-500. Reachy Mini, the open-source kit in the same band, is at /knowledge/how-much-is-reachy-mini. This page is with the other price answers at /knowledge/price. Open /wizard if you want the job, a desk companion, to pick the robot. The wizard will not hide the $279.

title: How much does Loona cost?
description: The catalog lists Loona at $439. The KEYi product page currently shows Premium at $409, down from a $529 list. Bundles cost more.
summary: Catalog price is $439, Buy Now. The official Premium page currently shows $409 against a $529 list. Bundles and the US shop can differ.
shortAnswer: HomeBotRadar lists Loona at $439, confirmed, Buy Now. The KEYi product page currently shows Loona Petbot Premium at $409, with $529 crossed out. Bundles and a separate US shop listing sit higher. There is no Vector-style membership required for the core pet. Check the store before you pay, and treat $439 as the tracked price.
content:
Loona is a wheeled pet from KEYi Tech. The catalog price is $439, confirmed. Status is Buy Now and available. The official Premium product page does not match that number today. It shows $409, with a $529 list crossed out, and it advertises a one-year warranty, support, and free shipping. The shop collection repeats $409 for Premium. Themed bundles on the same collection are higher. Buzzer Beater is listed at $468 against a $628 list, and Space Edition at $624 against $699. A separate US product URL has shown Premium near $639. Those are all KEYi pages, and they do not agree with each other.

## The catalog price stays $439

HomeBotRadar does not chase every promo. The tracked price stays $439 until an editor changes the row. This answer names the live page so you can see the gap. If you are about to pay, the checkout in your country is the number that matters. Tax, a bundle, and which storefront you opened can all move it. The $529 figure is a list price on the Premium page, not a second catalog sticker.

The robot itself is a small dog-shaped pet with a face, a camera, a depth sensor, and a dock it can return to. Chat features want Wi-Fi. Kids can program it with Blockly. KEYi says most of the sensing stays on the device. The catalog does not add a required monthly plan for the core pet, which is the split with Vector 2.0. Outfits, a second dock, and game props are optional and they are not inside the $439 line.

## Countries and the Vector comparison

Catalog countries for Loona include the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Canada, Australia, Singapore, and France. Shipping rules still belong to the store. A free-shipping line on a US page is not a promise for every country on that list. A collar, a ball, or an outfit can add a small second charge that never shows on the robot's price row.

Vector 2.0 is $249.99 for the hardware, then a voice membership if you want Hey Vector. Loona's promo price can land near Vector's hardware price, and the ongoing bill is the difference. See both at /compare/loona-vs-vector-2. The Vector plan is spelled out at /knowledge/does-vector-need-a-subscription. Pets you can buy are on /rankings/best-robot-pets. This page is at /knowledge/price. Open /wizard if you want a pet on the floor rather than a robot on a desk.

title: How much is Reachy Mini?
description: Reachy Mini starts at $399 for the Lite kit. The wireless kit is $499. Both are Buy Now, with lead time up to 90 days.
summary: Lite is $399 and needs your computer. Wireless is $499 and runs on its own. The catalog price is $399+.
shortAnswer: Reachy Mini Lite is $399 and tethers to your computer over USB. The wireless Reachy Mini is $499 and adds a Raspberry Pi, Wi-Fi, and a battery. The catalog price is $399+, confirmed, Buy Now. Lead time can run to 90 days. It is a desk kit you assemble, not a robot that walks the house.
content:
Reachy Mini is the open-source desk kit from Pollen Robotics, now part of Hugging Face. The catalog price is $399+, confirmed, Buy Now. The plus sign is there because two kits share the body and not the price. Lite is $399. It connects to a Mac, Linux, or Windows PC over USB, and the computer does the work. Wireless is $499. It adds a Raspberry Pi CM4, Wi-Fi, an IMU, and a 12.8 Wh battery so a demo can run without a laptop on the desk.

## The kit on the desk

You build the kit in about two hours. The head has six degrees of freedom, the body spins, and two antenna ears move. A wide camera and a four-microphone array face the room. Software includes a web dashboard, a simulator, ready-made behaviors, and Hugging Face Spaces apps. Hardware, firmware, and the SDK are open source under Apache 2.0. This is a robot you program. It is not a companion that arrives sealed and chats out of the box with no setup. Budget the afternoon, and a computer if you bought Lite.

Lead time is listed up to 90 days, and many orders ship sooner. The Pollen store ships to the European Union, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Canada. Other countries go through Seeed Studio. The catalog countries match that store list: United States, Canada, United Kingdom, and the European Union. A Seeed checkout can show a different total. The tracked prices stay $399 and $499. Neither kit includes a walking base. If you wanted a robot that crosses a room, this is the wrong row. The ears and the head are the whole body.

## Microduck is the other Pollen robot

Microduck is a 25 cm walking duck from the same company, with 15 motors and a grasping beak. The catalog price is $399, confirmed, and the status is Pre-order, aimed at Christmas 2026. Same dollar, different object. Reachy Mini is a head on a desk. Microduck is a small biped you wait for. The pair is /compare/microduck-vs-reachy-mini. Pay the kit you opened, Lite or wireless, and do not average them into one number.

Desktop robots under $500, scored as a best list, are on /rankings/best-desktop-robots-under-500. EMO, the $279 desk companion, is at /knowledge/how-much-is-emo. This page is at /knowledge/price. Open /wizard if you want a kit you can code rather than a pet. A kit price is the board and the motors, not a finished chore robot.

title: Can you pre-order Atom?
description: Atom is a Pre-order on the catalog. The tracked price is an estimate, $27,500 or more, from the China pre-sale. It is not a home cart like Unitree G1.
summary: Yes, as a pre-order. The catalog price is an estimate at $27,500 or more. Unitree G1 is the humanoid with a $13,500 cart.
shortAnswer: Atom is Pre-order on HomeBotRadar, with limited availability. The price is an estimate, $27,500 or more, tied to the China pre-sale around ¥199,000. It is Dobot's full-size humanoid, pitched for work demos as well as service floors. It is not the same kind of checkout as Unitree G1 at $13,500.
content:
You can start a pre-order for Atom. You cannot treat it as a finished home product with one global sticker. HomeBotRadar lists the status as Pre-order and the price as $27,500+, and the price status is an estimate. The figure comes from China pre-sales that opened around March 2025 near ¥199,000. Dobot's own US and China pages are the places a local quote will show up. If those pages print a different dollar amount, the catalog keeps $27,500+ until the row is edited, and the official page is the one named here. Ask which Atom you are reserving before you pay a deposit.

## The full-size humanoid

Atom is Dobot's first full-size humanoid, from the arm maker in Shenzhen. The walking flagship, Atom Max, is about 165 cm and roughly 58 kg without the hands, with 41 degrees of freedom once both dexterous hands are counted. Arms are rated around 3.5 kg, with a higher short peak. Published runtime is about two hours, and a charge is about an hour. Dobot also shows Atom D, a shorter dual-arm torso for data collection. That torso is not the walking robot. A pre-order conversation should name which configuration you mean.

The pitch is work: assembly, café, and pharmacy-style demos, plus a straight-knee walk. A demo aisle is not a promise that the robot will run your kitchen on the day it arrives. Countries on the catalog row are China, the United States, and Germany. Availability is limited. A pre-order in one of those countries still has to name the trim, the hand set, and who trains the robot after it arrives. HomeBotRadar does not turn a trade-fair walk into a delivery week.

## The humanoid with a cart

Unitree G1 is Buy Now at $13,500, often backordered, and that price is confirmed. It is smaller, about 132 cm, and it is sold as a developer platform. If the search is "humanoid I can pay for this week," the G1 is the row with a shop. Atom is the row with a pre-order and an estimate. The comparison is /compare/dobot-atom-vs-unitree-g1.

The G1 price is written out at /knowledge/how-much-is-the-unitree-g1. PM01, the other compact humanoid with a China list, is at /knowledge/how-much-is-the-pm01. Every humanoid we track, including Coming Soon and Discontinued, is on /rankings/best-humanoid-robots. This page is at /knowledge/buying. Open /wizard if the job is a home chore and a full-size pre-order is more robot than you need.

title: Where does NEO Gamma ship?
description: NEO Gamma is a United States pre-order. The order page still says US deliveries start in 2026. No other country is on the catalog row.
summary: The United States only. Delivery is a 2026 window, not a week. The price and the deposit are on the cost answer.
shortAnswer: NEO Gamma ships as a US pre-order. The catalog countries list is the United States, and the 1X order page still talks about 2026 US delivery. There is no published second country. A 2026 window is not a date on your door. The $20,000 and $499 plans, and the $200 deposit, are the price story, not a ship confirmation.
content:
NEO Gamma is listed for one country. The catalog row says United States. The order page is the same story: early-access ownership at $20,000 is described with priority 2026 US delivery, and the $499 a month plan is a later delivery. Both are pre-order language. Neither is a tracking number. A friend in another country cannot use your US place in line.

## A window, then a factory note

The order page still says US deliveries start in 2026. It does not name a month for your address. An April factory note said units coming off the line were prioritized for internal home testing. That sentence matters more than a map. A robot in the company's own houses is not a robot on a US truck. Until 1X names a customer shipment, the status stays Pre-order and availability stays limited. Internal testing can run for months without a customer date attached.

A shopper outside the United States should not translate the page into a local pre-order. There is no public euro price, no UK date, and no second flag on the catalog row. If 1X opens another country, the robot page is where that list changes. The deposit holds a place in the US line. It does not buy a shipping address in another country, and it does not move the robot ahead of the company's own test homes. One US address per place in line is the offer as written.

## Unitree G1 ships more widely, and it is a different product

Unitree G1 is Buy Now at $13,500. Catalog countries are the United States, China, Japan, and Germany. The shop is often backordered, and a backorder is still not the NEO delivery window. The G1 is a smaller humanoid sold for research and education. NEO Gamma is the soft-covered home pre-order. Sharing a year on a calendar does not make them the same shipment. The price, the height, and the status are on /compare/neo-gamma-vs-unitree-g1.

What you pay, including the deposit, is at /knowledge/neo-gamma-cost-and-ship-date. The G1 sticker is at /knowledge/how-much-is-the-unitree-g1. Stairs are not part of this ship answer. That question is at /knowledge/which-home-robots-climb-stairs. Humanoids with their real status are on /rankings/best-humanoid-robots. This page is the shipping shelf at /knowledge/shipping. Open /wizard if the country and the job should filter the catalog before you read another price. A filter will not invent a European NEO checkout. The order page is still a US page.

title: Is Doova for sale?
description: Doova is Coming Soon. Tuya has not published a price, a cart, or a ship date. ElliQ is the elder-care robot you can start in the US.
summary: No. Doova has no price and no cart. ElliQ is the US elder-care membership you can start now.
shortAnswer: No. Doova is Coming Soon. The price on the catalog is Unknown, and there is no consumer checkout or ship date. Tuya showed it at IFA 2026 as a wheeled companion for older adults who live alone. ElliQ is the elder-care robot with a US membership you can start now.
content:
Doova is not for sale. HomeBotRadar marks it Coming Soon, with a price of Unknown and availability Coming Soon. Tuya Smart showed the robot at IFA 2026 in Berlin. The company posts describe a short wheeled companion with no arms, a 10.1-inch screen, and a face, built for older adults living alone. They do not include a dollar price, a deposit, or a month when a customer robot ships. No waitlist form is the same thing as no sale.

## The IFA 2026 description

The intended day is a home, not a factory aisle. If you call for help, Doova is supposed to find you and, if you do not answer, start a video call to family. It is also described as a chatter, a reader, a reminder for medicine, and a voice remote for Tuya lights and appliances. While you are out, it can roll a room and send a safety report. It docks itself. Whole-home search for lost objects is listed as a later add-on, not a feature on a shipping unit. Those features are a product story. They are not a SKU.

None of that is a cart. A trade-show robot with a help phrase is still a plan until a shop asks for money and names a date. The catalog has no country list yet, because there is no offer to attach a country to. IFA 2026 is the public debut, not a ship quarter. Until Tuya prints a price, Doova stays on the coming-soon list and off the buy list.

## ElliQ is the one you can start

ElliQ is Buy Now in the United States as a membership. The catalog price is $250. The membership page is a lease: $249 to start, then $59 a month, $588 for 12 months, or $936 for 24 months. You do not keep the device when the plan ends. That is a real offer with real limits. It is also the reason Doova and ElliQ belong on the same compare. One is a coming senior companion with no sticker. The other is a US lease you can price today. See /compare/doova-vs-elliq.

The ElliQ dollars are at /knowledge/what-does-elliq-cost. Other robots with no cart are on /rankings/home-robots-coming-soon. This page is at /knowledge/buying. Open /wizard if you need something an older adult can start this month rather than a robot that is still on a stage. Coming Soon is a status, not a waitlist you can join.

title: How much is Isaac 1?
description: Isaac 1 is a US pre-order at $7,999, or $449 a month. A $250 deposit holds the place. California deliveries are aimed at fall 2026.
summary: Pay $7,999 or $449 a month. The deposit is $250 and refundable until it ships. California is first, in fall 2026.
shortAnswer: Isaac 1 is $7,999 up front, or $449 a month, on Weave Robotics' own page. A $250 deposit reserves a place and is refundable until the robot ships. Status on the catalog is Pre-order. First shipments are aimed at California in fall 2026, with the rest of the US through 2027.
content:
Isaac 1 has two home prices, and both are on the Weave Robotics product page. You can pay $7,999 up front, or $449 a month on the subscription. The order page asks for $250 today. That deposit reserves a place in line and is refundable any time until the robot ships. The catalog price is $7,999, confirmed. Status is Pre-order, and availability is limited. The monthly figure is the other official path. It is not a discount on the same checkout. Weave does not spell out the subscription length on the product page, so read the pre-order agreement before you treat $449 as a short rental.

## Who gets one first

The product page says first shipments begin in fall 2026. California comes first. Broader US availability follows through 2027. The catalog countries list is the United States. There is no European price on the page. After you pre-order, Weave says it will email you, and closer to delivery you can see the robot at a Weave location or on a video call. Commercial buyers are pointed to a separate contact. The home prices above are the home offer. A business quote is a different conversation and a different price.

Isaac 1 is a wheeled robot for laundry and resetting a room, not a biped. A remote operator can step in when it gets stuck. That is part of the product story on the company's own pages. A pre-order is still a pre-order. Fall 2026 is a season, not a week on a calendar you control. The deposit does not choose the payment plan. Weave says you settle buy-versus-subscribe as delivery gets close. Keep the agreement beside the $7,999 line so a monthly plan is not a surprise at the door.

## NEO Gamma is the other US pre-order

NEO Gamma is also a US pre-order, at $20,000 or $499 a month, with a $200 deposit and a 2026 delivery window. Isaac 1 is the wheeled home robot at $7,999. NEO Gamma is the humanoid. They share a country and a year, and they do not share a body or a price. The pair is /compare/isaac-1-vs-neo-gamma. Do not add the two deposits and call that a bundle.

Where NEO Gamma ships is at /knowledge/where-does-neo-gamma-ship. What it costs is at /knowledge/neo-gamma-cost-and-ship-date. Robots you can buy or pre-order are on /rankings/best-home-robots. This page is at /knowledge/price. Open /wizard if laundry and a wheeled base matter more than a humanoid shape.

title: How much is the PM01?
description: The catalog lists PM01 at $26,000, confirmed, Buy Now in China. The EngineAI shop shows ¥188,000.
summary: Catalog price is $26,000. The China shop lists ¥188,000. It is a developer humanoid, not a turnkey home robot.
shortAnswer: PM01 is $26,000 on the catalog, confirmed, Buy Now, with limited availability and China as the country. The EngineAI shop lists the same robot at ¥188,000. That yuan figure is the official sticker. The dollar figure is the tracked conversion. It is a compact research humanoid, not a chore robot with a US cart.
content:
PM01's official China shop lists ¥188,000. HomeBotRadar tracks that as $26,000, confirmed. Status is Buy Now, availability is limited, and the country on the row is China. If you can check out in yuan, the shop number is the one you pay. The dollar line is the catalog's conversion so the rest of the site can sort prices. It will not match a bank rate on the day you wire the money.

## The 2026 spec sheet

EngineAI describes PM01 as a lightweight, open humanoid for research, education, and demos. The 2026 education and navigation pages put it near 140 cm and about 44.5 kg with the battery, walking faster than 2 m/s, with a waist that turns past 300 degrees. Both trims list 24 joints, an 8-core CPU, a Jetson Orin NX, cameras at the head and waist, and about two hours on a 10,000 mAh pack. The navigation trim adds 3D LiDAR. Education keeps a chest screen and the secondary-dev access. An older FAQ on the same site once quoted ¥88,000. The buy page now shows ¥188,000. The catalog follows the current shop, not the old FAQ. Do not pay the old FAQ price.

Overseas buyers often meet a reseller quote instead of the China button. That quote can land in the same band and still is not the ¥188,000 button. Read the contract for warranty too. EngineAI has said the education trim carries a longer warranty than the commercial trim, and that the signed contract wins. A buy button in China is also not a promise of a US plug, a US manual, or a US service depot.

## Atom is the other pre-order humanoid

Atom is Pre-order at an estimated $27,500 or more, from Dobot's China pre-sale near ¥199,000. PM01 is the one with a China buy button and a yuan price. Atom is the one with an estimate and a pre-order status. Neither is a US home appliance. The pair is /compare/dobot-atom-vs-pm01. Whether you can start an Atom pre-order is at /knowledge/can-you-pre-order-dobot-atom. Bring the yuan figure to that compare, not a rumor of a US shelf price.

Unitree G1, at a confirmed $13,500, is the humanoid with the wider shop. Its price is at /knowledge/how-much-is-the-unitree-g1. The full humanoid list is on /rankings/best-humanoid-robots. This page is at /knowledge/price. Open /wizard if you need a robot for a home chore and a China dev platform is the wrong shelf.
